items.title: proxelar
items.author: Curator
items.content:
proxelar is both a CLI and TUI proxy that inspects and can capture and modify incoming HTTP, HTTPS and WebSocket traffic directly from your terminal.

Applications send traffic through proxelar's local proxy and it can extract displays headers, request bodies and individual streaming WebSocket frames. Like similar proxies, this terminal tool can also interactively Intercept pauses in HTTP requests for live editing before forwarding or dropping them with a custom response and captured requests can be replayed / repeated to the server.

proxelar has partial support for modern protocols such as HTTP/3, QUIC and Lua hooks can automate request and response changes, including returning mock responses from a reverse proxy. Sessions can be exported as HAR files or curl requests to be repeated or raw HTTP text requests.

Developers interested in network traffic analysis or security-focused engineers and researchers who need to test API behaviour by manipulating responses or requests can use proxelar to inspect traffic send from cilent-side applications or devices.

items.title: kernwatch
items.author: Curator
items.content:
kernwatch is a low-level Linux terminal monitor that focuses specifically on kernel activity and performance tracing.

It monitors the internal state of the running system kernel which displays detailed information on CPU scheduling, task memory, interrupts, cgroups and kernel modules inside of the system. eBPF captures allow kernwatch to measure wake delays, syscall durations and request latency with suitable kernel features and permissions.

In the 'flame' menu, it has a built-in profiler that allows you to select captures CPU stacks of running programs and compares their traced stacks with the saved baselines. Recording sessions are supported for offline replay of system activity and you can export them to preserve observations and diagnostic findings for later analysis.

kernwatch is for those who are performance engineering specialists, Linux administrators, system engineers and even Linux kernel developers that need a single terminal tool that assists with troubleshooting issues on their Linux machine and investigating low-level kernel issues.

items.title: termtastic
items.author: Curator
items.content:
termtastic is a terminal client for sending messages and inspecting Meshtastic radio networks.

It connects to a compatible Meshtastic device over connections such as Bluetooth LE, Wifi, LoRa or serial which it can automatically discover near-by devices on the network. You can reply and send reactions in channel chats and in direct conversations (DMs). All chats and connections made within the Meshtastic network are encrypted at the packet level including DMs that communicate through the network.

The node list in the TUI shows each connected node's statistics and telemetry information such as the signal readings, uptime, position, last-heard times and the last hop count. This terminal client allows for sorting and filtering for finding particular devices on the network and you can traceroute a node to show the packet's route through the mesh network. 

termtastic is for those who are engineers, developers or hobbyists in radio hardware or decentralised mesh networks who want to use a minimal terminal client to exchange messages and examine how neighbouring nodes connect through a mesh network regardless of the connection type.

items.title: spor
items.author: Curator
items.content:
spor watches your files while you work and saves a snapshot every time something changes, so every past state stays recoverable. Jump back to an earlier point and continue from there in a different direction, without losing the path you came from. Everything is automatic and local.

Auto-snapshots every file change into a branching history you move through freely, jumping back and forking off without losing any version. Drive it live from an interactive TUI or with one-shot commands. Local, deduplicated, compressed.

spor is for anyone whose work is exploratory rather than planned. Creative coders, designers, writers, data folks. Use it when you try things, back out, and try another direction, and don't want to lose any version you passed through.

items.title: sqlmux
items.author: Curator
items.content:
sqlmux is a TUI database client with split panes and edit safeguards with a Vim-style SQL editor.

The default layout is a 2-split pane with the open databases on the left and the results on the right or in separate tabs and it can connect to PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server and Redis connections in a shared tree. It has a read-only mode for dry-runs, which is useful for querying results before running them for real.

Additionally, it has auto-suggestions as you type and after executing them, it can suggest tables, columns and functions in the editor where table edits are staged until saving. It has a powerful command palette which displays a view of every quick action you can do to and can run Quick SQL statements from anywhere in the program.

This tool is useful to engineers, system administrators, database, backend developers and DevOps engineers who want an all-in-one terminal database client with strong permissions and safeguards built-in with a rich interface to access multiple DBs in the the terminal.

items.title: clavirio
items.author: Curator
items.content:
clavirio is a touch typing tester with tutor guided lessons and timed practice sessions inside of your terminal.

It has step-by-step lessons that introduce keys by finger pair and keyboard row. The lesson sequence supports keyboard layouts such as QWERTY, Dvorak and Colemak layouts which you can change at any time. A virtual keyboard below shows the corresponding finger position and the selected keys as you type the text that appears on the screen.

Practice typing modes include common words, programming terms, custom text and drills for weak keys. Live feedback displays typing speed, accuracy and errors. clavirio saves session histories and accuracy for individual keys and after each session, a results graph shows speed statistics and the weakest-key option with suggestions  for further practice.

For technical learners such as developers, technical writers or hobbyists that use the terminal can practice touch typing with visible keyboard movements and track their improvements over time.
